title: Card documents a position: relative that no stylesheet sets
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists
details:
`components/Card.md:60` gives the Card root `display: block` and `position: relative`.

`src/styles/components/card.css` contains no `position` declaration at all. The root class sets overflow, radius, border and shadow only.

A consumer who absolutely positions a badge or a menu inside a Card, on the strength of that line, gets it positioned against whichever ancestor does establish a containing block. That is usually the page rather than the card.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

Attempted and reverted, because the one-line fix is not visually inert. Adding `position: relative` to the Card root fails the visual gate at 90 of 94: `code-block` changes 1.79% and 1.82% of pixels, and `mermaid-diagram` 0.53% and 0.64%, in light and dark. The captures keep their dimensions, and no whole-pixel shift explains the difference: comparing the new render against the baseline at every offset from -2 to +2 in both axes, the smallest difference is at zero offset. So the text is rasterised differently rather than moved, which is what promoting the card to a containing block does to the subpixel positions of its descendants. Accepting the fix means re-recording four captures for a containing block nothing in the library currently uses. Correcting the specification instead costs nothing and leaves a consumer without the anchor. That is a decision for the repository owner.
